tagline: Read-it-later app with highlights, RSS, PDFs, and spaced review.
verdictSummary: A self-hosted reading app — save an article by URL, extract clean text, highlight passages, export everything to Markdown — is a real weekend build covering the daily-use core. What doesn't come with it is Readwise's actual depth: mature parsing across difficult sites, RSS and PDF ingestion, Kindle integration, and a spaced-repetition review system.
coreLoopDIY: Save articles by URL through a bookmarklet, extract clean readable text, highlight passages, and export everything to Markdown on a schedule so nothing stays trapped in the app.
whatYouLose: parsing quality tuned across years of difficult websites
whyPeopleStillPay: All of someone's reading inputs — articles, Kindle highlights, PDFs, RSS — flow into one durable highlight system; people pay for that consolidation, not for highlighting text itself.
notes: A useful example: the DIY version covers the daily-use core quickly, but the wider ingestion ecosystem is where power users actually get their value.
prompt:
Build a personal read-it-later app: a bookmarklet posts the current page's URL to your server, which extracts clean readable text and stores the title, author, site, and cleaned content — falling back to just the bare link with a clear 'source only' badge when extraction fails, rather than mangling the page. Build a reading view with an estimated read time and select-to-highlight, storing each highlight with its surrounding context. Organize saved articles into an inbox, an archive, and tag-based lists. Build a highlights page grouped by article, with a scheduled export of everything to dated Markdown files so highlights outlive the app regardless of what happens to it. Add full-text search across both articles and highlights.

Do not build RSS ingestion, PDF or ebook parsing, Kindle sync, or mobile apps — the browser and the bookmarklet are the entire capture surface here, and that's the honest, complete scope for a personal tool.

faq.q: Can I import my existing Readwise Reader library?
faq.a: Readwise lets you export your highlights, and a short script can convert that export into this build's format. The original article HTML and reading position generally don't come across, only the saved highlights.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: As a responsive web page, yes, for reading and highlighting, but there's no offline mode and no dedicated mobile app — you need a network connection to reach it.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting and a database, typically a few dollars a month.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Spaced-repetition review. Readwise resurfaces old highlights on a schedule designed to help you actually retain them; this build exports highlights to files but doesn't decide when to show you which ones again.
